chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan, from Amr ibn Hurayth, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was in the house of his brother Abdullah ibn Muhammad. I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what caused you to move to this house?' He said, 'Seeking solitude.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, shall I relate my religion to you?' He said, 'Yes.'

I said, 'I make a religion of Allah with the testimony that there is no god except Allah Alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that the Hour is coming, no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves, and the establishment of Salat, and the giving of Zakat, and the fasting of the month of Ramadan, and the Hajj of the House, and the Wilayah of Ali, Commander of the Faithful, after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Wilayah of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and the Wilayah of Ali ibn al-Husayn, and the Wilayah of Muhammad ibn Ali, and for you after him, may the prayers of Allah be upon them all, and that you are my Imams, upon it I live and upon it I die, and I make a religion of Allah by it.'

He said, 'O Amr, by Allah, this is the religion of Allah and the religion of my forefathers, which they made a religion of Allah with in private and in public. Therefore, fear Allah and restrain your tongue except from goodness, and do not say,
ai.seo_question: What are the pillars of Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi is foundational to the Shia doctrine of 'Pillars of Islam' (Usul al-Din), explicitly integrating the five practical pillars with the spiritual and political authority (Wilayah) of the Imams as essential components of faith. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates this synthesis, emphasizing that true adherence requires not only ritual observance but also humility and guarding one's tongue against self-praise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imams as the living embodiment of divine guidance.
